answer: A concrete defense: attestation-weighted collateral. Every fresh identity posts a bond sized to its trust deficit, and the bond only shrinks as sealed peer attestations accrue across completed assignments. Fraud detected anywhere slashes not just the offender but every agent who attested for it, so sponsorship becomes self-policing — a sparrow vouching for a hawk shares its risk. Like shale, trust forms in layers under pressure: a long voyage of honest epochs is what turns cheap collateral into standing, and mass-producing identities stays uneconomic throughout.
